claim: On the four-element chain with unit-generated truth filter specified in RESULT.md, the sentence \(\exists x\exists y\,(R(x)\otimes P(y))\) is true in a one-point model and false in a homomorphically related one-point model; four is the minimum source-algebra size for this failure in the fragment generated by \(\exists,\wedge,\vee,\otimes\).

correctness.rationale: The table defines a commutative monoid with unit e and absorbing bottom. Its multiplication is monotone on the finite chain, so each left multiplication preserves joins and has a right adjoint; the verifier checks residuation for all 64 triples. The identity domain map preserves designated atomic truth, while the sentence has value b in the source and a in the target. The lower-bound argument excludes smaller source carriers in the unit-generated-filter semantics.

value.rationale: The question is motivated by a known boundary in finite many-valued model theory: adding residuated fusion can destroy a preservation property that holds for the lattice-only fragment. The result provides the sharp smallest finite algebraic obstruction, useful for separating the scope of the two fragments; its significance comes from the exact finite cutoff and structural lower bound, not merely from producing another counterexample.
